history.dynasty: Jadeja (built under Jam Rawal, founder of Jamnagar)
history.period: Mid-16th century, during the rule of Jam Rawal (verify - exact date not established)
history.summary: The Bhidbhanjan Temple in Patrakar Colony, opposite the Jamnagar Municipal Corporation, is one of the ancient Shiva temples of Jamnagar, dedicated to Bhidbhanjan Mahadev. It was constructed during the rule of Jam Rawal, the Jadeja founder of the city (traditionally 1540). The temple is best known for its Hindu-Rajput style of architecture: the walls and pillars carry exquisite carvings, the doors feature intricate silver work, and the shikhara is inspired by the architecture of South Indian temple towers. It is an oasis of divinity in the heart of the city, attracting large crowds during the holy month of Shravan. There are also 10 small shrines dedicated to various Hindu gods including Goddess Parvati and Lord Ganapati, and devotees believe chanting the Mrutyunjay Mahadev mantra here is especially beneficial.

name: Bhidbhanjan Temple, Jamnagar
town_description: Jamnagar is a coastal city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, on the Gulf of Kutch, founded in 1540 by Jam Rawal of the Jadeja Rajput clan as Nawanagar. Nicknamed 'Chhoti Kashi' (Little Kashi) for its many temples, it is a major pilgrim and tourist hub whose landmarks include Lakhota Lake, the Lakhota Palace museum and the Bala Hanuman temple. The city is also an industrial centre, home to one of the world's largest oil refining complexes at nearby Motikhavdi.

travel.railway: Jamnagar railway station, about 4 km away (per trawell.in).
travel.road: In Patrakar Colony opposite the Jamnagar Municipal Corporation; city buses, autos and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan month and Mondays draw the largest crowds; best time for aarti is usually 7 PM (verify).
